subject: pharmacology
title: Nitrates: Nitroglycerin, Isosorbide and Nitrate Tolerance

steps.tx: Sublingual **nitroglycerin** (glyceryl trinitrate) aborts an angina attack in one to three minutes because the rich sublingual venous drainage bypasses hepatic first pass destruction that swallows most of an oral dose. Inside smooth muscle it is denitrated to nitric oxide, cyclic GMP rises, myosin light chains dephosphorylate and the vessel relaxes. Tablets degrade with light, air and moisture, so patients replace opened bottles regularly and expect a tingle that confirms potency.
steps.say: Under the tongue, nitroglycerin works in minutes because it dodges the liver on its way to the veins.

nodes.label: Sublingual nitroglycerin absorbed directly to systemic veins
Nitric oxide released in vascular smooth muscle
Cyclic GMP rises, myosin light chain dephosphorylated

steps.tx: Sublingual **nitroglycerin**, also called glyceryl trinitrate, stops an angina attack in one to three minutes because sublingual veins drain straight into the systemic circulation and skip the hepatic first pass that destroys most of a swallowed dose. In smooth muscle the drug is denitrated to nitric oxide, cyclic GMP rises, myosin light chains lose phosphate, and the vessel relaxes. Venodilatation cuts preload and wall tension, which lowers myocardial oxygen need. Opened tablets spoil in light, air, and moisture, and a lingual tingle confirms the tablet is still active.
steps.say: Nitroglycerin under the tongue aborts angina in one to three minutes because that blood skips the liver. Nitric oxide raises cyclic GMP, myosin light chains are dephosphorylated, and smooth muscle relaxes. Wider veins lower preload and wall tension. Tablets decay with light, air, and moisture, and a tingle under the tongue shows the bottle is still potent.

vis.alt: Sublingual nitroglycerin entering venous blood, dilating veins, and lowering cardiac preload and wall tension.
vis.caption: A tablet under the tongue sends nitrate into venous blood, veins widen, and ventricular filling pressure falls. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: Nitrates dilate veins far more than arteries at clinical doses, so their antianginal magic is mainly **preload** reduction: blood pools in capacitance veins, ventricular filling and wall tension fall, and myocardial oxygen demand drops to meet the fixed supply. Coronary dilatation helps at stenoses and in spasm, but demand reduction explains relief even when a rigid atherosclerotic artery cannot dilate at all.
steps.say: Nitrates rest the heart by pooling blood in veins and cutting wall tension, not mainly by opening the blocked artery.

left.title: Demand side gains
points: Venodilatation pools blood in capacitance vessels
Preload, chamber size and wall tension fall
Oxygen demand drops toward the fixed supply
Subendocardial perfusion improves as diastolic pressure falls

right.title: Supply side gains
points: Epicardial coronary segments dilate, even at stenoses
Collateral flow to ischaemic zones improves
Coronary spasm is directly antagonised
Platelet aggregation modestly inhibited by nitric oxide

steps.tx: An intravenous nitrate infusion titrated against pain and pressure serves **unstable angina** and acute heart failure, while the spray suits patients whose tablets have expired mid attack. Failure of three sublingual doses at five minute intervals is not a dosing problem but a triage signal: the patient needs an emergency department, aspirin and an infarction workup. Headache, flushing and postural dizziness are the everyday costs of cerebral and cutaneous vasodilatation.
steps.say: Three doses without relief means hospital, not a fourth dose; headache and flushing are the usual toll.

vis.alt: Acute coronary syndrome pathophysiology showing plaque disruption and thrombus formation
vis.caption: Acute coronary syndrome pathophysiology; pain persisting after three nitrate doses is managed on this pathway, not with more nitrate.

steps.tx: For prevention rather than rescue, **isosorbide mononitrate** is the orally reliable workhorse: it is the active metabolite of isosorbide dinitrate, escapes the variable first pass activation its parent needs, and gives predictable levels once or twice daily. Isosorbide dinitrate itself is still used, including with hydralazine in heart failure, but variable conversion between patients makes the mononitrate the tidier examination and prescribing answer.
steps.say: Mononitrate is the predictable oral nitrate; the dinitrate needs liver activation that varies between patients.

left.title: Isosorbide mononitrate
points: Active as swallowed, no activation step needed
Complete, predictable oral bioavailability
Once or twice daily prophylaxis dosing
Needs a daily nitrate free interval built in

right.title: Isosorbide dinitrate
points: Prodrug converted to mononitrate in the liver
Variable bioavailability between patients
Partner to hydralazine in heart failure regimens
Sublingual form can rescue attacks, slower than nitroglycerin

steps.tx: Continuous nitrate exposure bleaches its own effect within 24 hours, the phenomenon of **nitrate tolerance**: sulfhydryl groups needed to generate nitric oxide are depleted, oxidative stress scavenges what is made, and reflex neurohormonal activation fights back. Transdermal patches worn around the clock fail by the second day, which astonished early users. Sensitivity returns after ten to twelve hours without nitrate, so every chronic regimen is built around a daily free interval.
steps.say: Round the clock nitrate stops working within a day; tolerance is pharmacology, not the patient imagining it.

nodes.label: Reflex renin and sympathetic activation adds opposition
Antianginal effect fades: nitrate tolerance established

steps.tx: Prescribers engineer the **free interval** rather than fight tolerance: patches come off overnight, mononitrate is dosed asymmetrically at 8 am and 2 pm, and dinitrate skips the evening dose. The unprotected window is placed when angina is least likely, usually asleep, and covered by a beta blocker or calcium channel blocker in exertional disease. Escalating the nitrate dose to bulldoze tolerance only deepens it.
steps.say: Schedule the nitrate free window overnight and cover it with another class; never escalate through tolerance.

left.title: Regimens that preserve effect
points: Patch on by day, off for 10 to 12 hours overnight
Mononitrate at 8 am and 2 pm, none in the evening
Beta blocker or calcium blocker covers the gap
Free interval timed to the patient's quiet hours

right.title: Regimens that destroy effect
points: Patch left on continuously for days
Even eight hourly oral dosing around the clock
Dose escalation chasing a fading response
Intravenous infusion beyond 24 hours without review

steps.tx: Explosives workers taught medicine this pharmacology first: chronic factory exposure produced tolerance all week, then withdrawal angina and even infarction on days away, christened **Monday disease** as symptoms struck on returning after the weekend break had restored sensitivity and exposure resumed. The story is more than colour; it demonstrates dependence of vascular tone on exogenous nitrate and warns that abrupt withdrawal of long infusions can rebound coronary tone.
steps.say: Monday disease in explosives workers proved tolerance and withdrawal spasm decades before patches repeated the lesson.

nodes.label: Week long factory nitrate exposure builds tolerance
Monday re exposure and withdrawal swings provoke symptoms
Lesson: taper long infusions, never stop abruptly

steps.tx: Two interactions can crash pressure: nitrates with **sildenafil** or any phosphodiesterase 5 inhibitor multiply cyclic GMP from both production and breakdown sides, and nitrates within 24 hours of sildenafil or 48 hours of tadalafil are contraindicated. Separately, nitrates in right ventricular infarction or severe aortic stenosis remove the preload those circulations depend on. Both scenarios headline the companion lesson on sildenafil interaction and variant angina.
steps.say: Nitrate plus sildenafil can collapse pressure; preload dependent hearts collapse on nitrates alone. Both are examination favourites.

left.title: Dangerous combinations
points: Sildenafil within 24 hours, tadalafil within 48 hours
Riociguat: absolute contraindication with nitrates
Alcohol and other vasodilators add postural falls
Volume depleted patients faint on standing doses

right.title: Dangerous circulations
points: Right ventricular infarction depends on preload
Severe aortic stenosis cannot raise output to compensate
Hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy worsens
Inferior infarction with bradycardia: dose with caution
